author: Esteban L. Hernandez
title: Colorado set to receive $615M from Meta settlement - NewsBreak
text:
By Esteban L. Hernandez Nathan Bomey ,
12 hours ago
Colorado is set to receive nearly $615 million from the landmark $17 billion Meta settlement over allegations Facebook and Instagram were designed in ways that harm children.
Why it matters: This is social media's version of the landmark 1990s tobacco settlement — effectively reshaping the industry and the way young Americans experience some of their favorite platforms.
Zoom in: The 47-state settlement will resolve claims against the company and bring Colorado roughly $615 million over nine years, Attorney General Phil Weiser said in a statement.
The money will go toward "protecting and restoring" mental health and safety for Colorado kids. What they're saying: "The relief we are getting in this settlement is very meaningful and well beyond what any court has ordered or is likely to order," Weiser said.
Caveat: The agreement is subject to court approval.
Driving the news: Meta agreed to provide compensation for a variety of public health purposes, including crisis intervention, after-school programs, outdoor activities and youth mental health programming.
Meta also agreed to limited under-18 users to 2 hours per day on Facebook and Instagram, block them from accessing the platforms from midnight to 6am, and limit notifications during school hours. Young people will also be given the option to have a chronological feed, not an algorithmic one — and parents can make it the default option. Kids also won't be able to see likes or other post reactions. Full story
